module.purpose: Provides a Redux middleware handler builder that batches RTK Query subscription actions to optimize performance by mutating internal maps and throttling store syncs.
module.summary: This file exports a factory that creates a middleware handler managing subscription state for RTK Query. It maintains internal nested Maps of subscriptions, directly mutates them for performance, and periodically syncs a serialized copy to the Redux store via a throttled timer. It intercepts specific actions to update subscriptions and exposes selectors for hooks.
module.businessContext: RTK Query middleware subscription batching; critical for performance and DevTools visibility. Failure causes excessive dispatches or stale subscription state.

units.name: actuallyMutateSubscriptions

detail.name: actuallyMutateSubscriptions
preconditions: currentSubscriptions is a mutable Map-like structure supporting get, set, delete, and has operations.
action is a well-formed Redux-style action carrying the payload and/or meta fields expected by whichever action creator's .match() returns true.
postconditions: Returns true when the action matches updateSubscriptionOptions, unsubscribeQueryResult, removeQueryResult, or queryThunk.pending.
Returns true when the action matches queryThunk.rejected AND meta.condition is truthy AND meta.arg.subscribe is true.
Returns false when the action matches queryThunk.rejected but meta.condition is falsy or meta.arg.subscribe is falsy, or when the action matches no handled type.
For queryThunk.pending, always gets-or-inserts the substate map entry for arg.queryCacheKey, but only sets a requestId->options entry when arg.subscribe is truthy.
edgeCases: updateSubscriptionOptions with no existing subscription map for queryCacheKey or no existing requestId entry: silently returns true without any mutation.
unsubscribeQueryResult with no existing subscription map for queryCacheKey: silently returns true without any mutation.
queryThunk.pending with arg.subscribe falsy: gets-or-inserts the substate map but does not set a subscription entry; still returns true.
queryThunk.rejected with meta.condition falsy: no subscription mutation occurs, returns false.
queryThunk.rejected with meta.condition truthy but meta.arg.subscribe falsy: no subscription mutation occurs, returns false.
Action matches none of the handled .match() predicates: falls through to the rejected-check block which also fails to match, returns false with no state mutation.
stateMutations: Mutates entries within the currentSubscriptions Map: get-or-insert of inner Map for a queryCacheKey (via getOrInsertComputed with createNewMap), set of a requestId->options entry within an inner Map, delete of a requestId entry within an inner Map, and delete of an entire queryCacheKey entry from the outer Map.
detail.summary: Processes a Redux action to mutate the internal subscriptions state map for RTK Query subscriptions. Returns true when the action matches a handled mutation type (including queryThunk.pending and conditional queryThunk.rejected cases), and false for unhandled or non-mutating rejected actions.

detail.name: isRequestSubscribed
postconditions: Returns true if a subscription entry exists for both queryCacheKey and requestId in the subscriptions map; returns false otherwise
Does not throw regardless of whether getSubscriptions() returns undefined, null, or a Map missing either key
edgeCases: When getSubscriptions() returns undefined or null, the optional chaining short-circuits and returns false without throwing
When the queryCacheKey is not present in the subscriptions Map, returns false
When the requestId is not present for the given queryCacheKey in the inner Map, returns false
When both keys exist and the inner value is falsy (e.g. null, undefined, 0, empty string), the double-negation coerces to false

errorPolicy.onInvalidInput: No errors thrown — null-safe optional chaining handles all undefined/null and missing-key paths by returning false

Returns true if both the queryCacheKey and requestId exist in the subscriptions structure, false otherwise, without throwing on any null or missing-key path.

detail.name: serializeSubscriptions
preconditions: currentSubscriptions is a valid SubscriptionInternalState (nested Maps with string keys)
The function relies on JSON.stringify correctly serializing all values within the Maps
postconditions: Returns a SubscriptionState object with the same structure as the input but using plain objects instead of Maps
All keys and values from the original Maps are preserved in the returned object
The returned object contains no Map instances
invariants: The structure of the returned object matches the shape of the input nested Maps
String keys in the Maps remain string keys in the resulting objects
edgeCases: Empty currentSubscriptions Map results in an empty object in the returned structure
Nested empty Maps result in empty objects at the corresponding level
Values that are not natively JSON-serializable will be omitted or converted (e.g., undefined becomes null)
Map iteration order is preserved in the resulting object property insertion order

errorPolicy.onInvalidInput: JSON.stringify throws a TypeError if it encounters a circular reference or non-serializable value

detail.ioFormatSpec: Transforms nested Map<string, Map<string, unknown>> into { [key: string]: { [key: string]: unknown } } via JSON roundtrip and Object.fromEntries conversion
detail.summary: Converts a nested subscription Map structure into a plain object hierarchy suitable for JSON serialization and storage.
